A novel method for calculating shadows in complex scenes with objects of varying detail levels is presented. This technique leverages a simplified model of high-resolution geometry, coupled with a detailed representation of low-resolution geometry, to efficiently compute shadows. By utilizing ray marching on the low-resolution geometry model and incorporating information about high-resolution geometry, accurate shadows can be calculated without the need for ray tracing. This approach yields a significant reduction in computational cost, allowing for the real-time rendering of shadows on complex geometry models.

In probabilistic O-D demand modeling, a multi-nomial probit model is commonly used, which involves estimating a high-dimensional covariance matrix from origin-destination demand and link travel times. Due to the significant number of zones, the covariance matrix dimensionality is typically very large, exceeding the number of samples available for estimation. This situation leads to an under-determined problem, which can be addressed by employing a high regularization penalty in Lasso estimation. The resulting sparse covariance matrix not only facilitates interpretation but also enables efficient sampling. The effectiveness of Lasso in producing a well-structured covariance matrix is demonstrated through a numerical example, which shows its ability to yield a dimensionally-reduced matrix that can be efficiently sampled using a Cholesky decomposition.

This study investigates the impact of non-linear frequency characteristics in a population-synchronized group of weakly linked phase oscillators. We demonstrate that frequency non-linearities can lead to the emergence of stable, synchronized states that persist even in the presence of frequency variations and stochastic disturbances. We derive an equation that accurately describes the slow time evolution of these synchronized states and show that they can be stable under certain conditions, even in the absence of non-linear coupling. We also examine the effects of noise and frequency instability on these synchronized states, finding that they can be stable up to a certain level of noise intensity. Our research provides a theoretical framework for understanding and designing weakly linked oscillator systems with non-linear frequency characteristics.

We have developed an innovative algorithm that efficiently creates a uniform spanning tree of a given graph, by combining and enhancing two existing algorithms - one based on deep learning and the other on random walks. By leveraging the strengths of both methods, the new algorithm significantly accelerates sampling speeds, particularly for large graphs, while maintaining unbiased results. Furthermore, we have created a specialized library for deep learning-driven algorithm implementation.

Music representation learning has gained significant attention in recent years,
particularly in applications that connect audio and text data.  However, the
availability of large music datasets with multi-modal annotations is limited,
hindering the development of comprehensive benchmarks.  To address this
shortcoming, we introduce MusicTM-50K, an expansive music dataset comprising
50,000 entries with text and audio metadata.  This dataset not only facilitates
cross-modal retrieval but also enables classification and clustering analysis.
We propose a novel method that leverages the dataset to produce accurate music
captions and audio descriptions, and through comparison with existing models,
we demonstrate the dataset's potential to enhance music representation
learning.  MusicTM-50K is freely accessible at https://github.com/
saharshahabi/Music-Representation-Learning.

Visualizing and analyzing vast amounts of interconnected data, such as that found in Wikidata, can be challenging due to the sheer volume of information and limited understanding of the underlying data model. Our proposed solution, Ontodia, is a visual exploration tool that allows users to create and apply custom filters based on their knowledge of the data ontology. By leveraging the data's inherent structure, Ontodia enhances data comprehension and enables efficient exploration of large knowledge bases. A case study on Wikidata demonstrates the benefits of using a knowledge graph for data exploration and understanding.

This study presents Lotse, a software library that facilitates the implementation of various guidance strategies. Built using Python, Lotse offers a versatile platform for developing and testing different methods of guiding objects along desired paths. The library's modular design enables seamless integration with other tools, such as model predictive control, to optimize and adapt guidance in real-time. Lotse includes multiple pre-implemented guidance methods, such as a model-based approach for following curved paths and a terminal guidance technique for smooth object stops. The library's capabilities are demonstrated through practical examples, showcasing its effectiveness in achieving desired guidance outcomes.

A comprehensive simulation study of the relaxed nested flux surface configuration, 
achieved through the use of external control coils, has been conducted using the 
JEDI code. The impact of a single control coil positioned at various radii on 
the tokamak's edge has been examined, and the results indicate that optimal coil 
placement is crucial for minimizing the coil's required strength and maintaining 
the desired nested flux surface structure. The placement of the control coil 
significantly influences the volume and flexibility of the nested flux surfaces, 
and coils placed closer to the center of the tokamak can produce more complex 
structures. The study also explores the implications of these findings for the 
design of magnetic configurations in tokamaks.

A new, highly accurate method for measuring temperature in reactors has been developed. This method relies on tracking the temperature-dependent shift in proton resonance frequency, which can be done using a reference signal. By utilizing a two-dimensional free induction decay measurement, researchers can obtain precise results. A laboratory-scale reactor was tested with a mixture of water and sodium nitrate, and the findings showed that the new method can achieve temperature accuracy within 0.1 degrees Celsius over a range of 10 to 30 degrees Celsius.

We investigate the conditions under which multiple distinct condensates can form when combining $N$ different species of bosons in a system with attractive forces. The system is governed by a mathematical model that describes the behavior of these bosons. The study reveals that the number of unique condensates that can form is directly related to the number of species involved, and this number grows linearly with the number of species. The mathematical model can be translated into a problem of finding optimal solutions for a specific type of energy function, known as a quadratic function, in a space of $N$ dimensions. The solution to this problem is found to be directly related to the properties of a special type of matrix that describes the interactions between the bosons. The solution also reveals the conditions under which multiple distinct condensates can form and their stability. The findings have implications for understanding the behavior of bosons in systems with attractive forces and may be relevant to studies of cold atoms and photonic systems.

The occurrence of magnetic field line breakups in solar flares can trigger rapid magnetic field variations, which move at high speeds within the solar atmosphere.  To study these phenomena, researchers used the high-resolution Solar Dynamics Observatory/Athena instrument to observe a specific solar flare event on May 10, 2014, which originated from a particular solar region.  By analyzing the data, researchers identified several magnetic field variations, which were observed moving at speeds ranging from 10 to 20 kilometers per second within the solar atmosphere.  These magnetic field variations were found to originate from the center of a particular solar feature and were influenced by the solar flare activity.  These magnetic field variations were found to correlate with a specific type of solar flare activity known as type III bursts.  These findings provide important insights into the behavior of the solar atmosphere during flares and can help scientists better understand the solar atmosphere.

We offer a new proof of the Madsen-Weiss theorem by combining two key ideas: a `b`-principle along with `b`-stability thm's. This involves showing that certain modified versions of moduli spaces of surfaces grow in a predictable manner as their complexity increases. Ultimately, this `b`-stability leads to the desired result through an analysis of topological intersection pairings.

We provide a detailed analytical breakdown of the BDDC algorithm's performance, 
offering explicit bounds for its eigenvalue distribution in relation to various 
parameters. These bounds are also shown to be reasonably close to actual 
distributions in practice.

This study investigates the dynamics of Tagging Systems, examining how users apply and modify these labels in an effort to comprehend and predict their behavior. By analyzing these changes, we can devise more effective mechanisms for organizing and retrieving information. Our research focuses on the evolution of Twitter hashtags over time, revealing that their usage patterns are influenced by both short-term trends and lasting popularity. This insight enables the creation of a more refined metric for measuring a hashtag's relevance, balancing its current frequency with its historical significance.

Acoustic metamaterials with tailored properties can be designed using tiny structures, but their performance at the microscopic level is influenced by temperature and viscosity effects that need to be considered. To address this, we investigated the impact of these effects on a specific acoustic metamaterial composed of a porous layer and tiny spherical objects, using a detailed simulation method. The results showed significant deviations from expected behavior under certain conditions, indicating that traditional design methods may not be suitable in specific applications, such as medical procedures.

We examine the four-dimensional FENE dumbbell model under the assumption of low frequency, resulting in the removal of the singularity in the spring coefficient. This allows for the establishment of a global weak solution in a specific type of spaces, combining Sobolev and Lebesgue spaces. Furthermore, under the condition of low frequency, the model's solutions exhibit regularity in a specific type of spaces, known as Besov spaces, and these solutions also demonstrate a certain degree of smoothness in time.

This study investigates the performance of mobile networks using integrated access and backhaul technology, where base stations provide user connectivity while also connecting to the core network via this mode. By simulating a scenario with multiple clusters of users moving in specific patterns, we assess the impact of these technologies on connectivity and latency under various conditions. Our results show that traditional network designs fail to keep up with the needs of moving groups, but a mobile network using IAB and backhaul technology can adapt to their movement, delivering improved connectivity and lower latency.

This study investigates the stability of algorithm performance in relation to changes in hyperparameters. We demonstrate the existence of interdependent relationships between these settings, where altering one set impacts the effectiveness of another set. Our analysis reveals that the proportion of such dependent relationships increases as the number of sets of parameters grows. To address this, we propose a new set of hyperparameters that are not influenced by changes in other sets, allowing for more efficient optimization. Our findings show that the proposed method significantly reduces the number of required hyperparameter sets, with a notable improvement in optimization efficiency.

A detailed explanation of the hydrogen spectrum's Balmer series, the electromagnetic field's energy quantization, and the photon concept is provided, with references to specific experimental evidence supporting the photon concept.

Reinforcement learning has achieved significant breakthroughs in complex tasks, but its practical application is hindered by the high cost of real-world interactions. A more efficient approach to learning, known as curriculum learning, has been proposed to improve sample efficiency. However, the lack of a unified framework for designing curricula hampers the development of robust and generalizable curriculum learning algorithms. To address this issue, we introduce a comprehensive library called Curricula, which provides a wide range of modular curriculum designs for benchmark environments. Our library enables the evaluation of RL algorithms under controlled curriculum changes and facilitates the discovery of new designs through automated search methods. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the importance of curriculum design in RL and showcase the versatility of our library in supporting the development of innovative curriculum designs.

Liger is a sophisticated, cross-platform system that seamlessly integrates with the LSST Data Management system and the LCO Global Observatory. This project aims to automate the process of searching for transient phenomena, such as supernovae and transiting objects, by analyzing astronomical images. Operating as a distributed computing service, Liger is capable of scanning multiple images simultaneously to detect new events. Currently, the system is operational and has been successfully used to monitor a variety of celestial objects from the LCO's 1-meter telescopes.

We demonstrate the presence of an infinite number of non-trivial traveling wave patterns that emerge in close proximity to the Couette flow, specifically in scenarios where the domain's aspect ratio is exceedingly small. Our findings are based on the assumption that these waves exhibit a certain level of smoothness just above a threshold of $H^4$. The analysis also reveals the existence of an infinite number of spatial oscillations in these patterns, with their amplitudes decreasing at a rate proportional to the domain's aspect ratio. The solution's structure is characterized by a combination of the Couette flow and a series of oscillatory modes, with each mode's amplitude decaying at a rate proportional to the domain's aspect ratio. The first mode's amplitude is linearly proportional to the domain's aspect ratio, while all subsequent modes' amplitudes are quadratic or higher order in the domain's aspect ratio. The derivation of these waves relies on the construction of a series of approximate solutions, with each mode's amplitude determined by a series of integrals involving the velocity and pressure fields. The first mode's amplitude is determined by a series of integrals involving the velocity field, with the first integral being non-zero. The higher order modes' amplitudes are determined by a series of integrals involving the velocity and pressure fields, with the first integral being zero. The existence of these waves is also confirmed in the case where the domain's aspect ratio is very small.

A groundbreaking method of controlling polarization is being explored, with far-reaching implications for applications in spintronics, non-linear optics and quantum information technology. Our research reveals that an innovative approach can give rise to a form of cross-talk between different components of the Stokes vector, resulting in the creation of an effective "polarization lattice" that enables a diverse range of polarization control capabilities.

We provide a detailed solution to a one-dimensional, one-parameter generalized Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equation that incorporates a fractional Laplacian and a multiplicative noise, resulting in a stochastic partial differential equation. This is achieved by developing a stochastic convolution technique that satisfies key properties, along with a novel localization approach for handling the nonlinearity. The equation's behavior is then examined for different values of its λ parameter, revealing distinct patterns of solution existence and non-existence, as well as a new stochastic integration by parts formula in the case of λ greater than one.

The COVID-19 pandemic has brought about significant changes in daily life, and countries are adapting to the crisis in various ways. In South Africa, limited and unreliable data has hindered the COVID-19 response efforts, and the government's COVID-19 task force website is the primary source of information, but it lacks real-time data and is difficult to access. This study aims to develop a data pipeline to collect, process, and visualize data from the South African government's website to support researchers, data analysts, and the general public. The pipeline will enable the creation of dashboards to monitor the pandemic's progression and will be used to analyze data from the South African government's website.

This passage discusses a modified version of Szemeredi's Theorem tailored for subsets comprising limited-size unions of geometric series with varying density, and also explores an analogous result for summands, and provides an illustrative example of a dense subset lacking limited-depth structured patterns, such as groups, decreasing sequences, and increasing sequences.

In the domain of multi-modal learning, the integration of information from various sources is a critical issue. Current approaches to this problem can be categorized into three methods: early, intermediate, and hierarchical fusion. While early and intermediate fusion methods are prevalent, they often struggle with the dimensionality of input data and the loss of information due to the need for a common representation. In contrast, hierarchical fusion, which remains underutilized, allows information to be preserved by merging data on multiple levels. This paper presents a hierarchical fusion framework for person re-identification that combines image and place data, demonstrating its effectiveness in experiments conducted on the person2person dataset.

The COVID-19 pandemic has overwhelmed healthcare systems globally, necessitating effective resource allocation to manage the surge of patients. To address this challenge, we have developed a predictive model that can identify patients at risk of requiring ICU admission based on specific features. By understanding which characteristics are most influential in predicting ICU admission, we can tailor our testing and monitoring efforts to prioritize high-risk individuals. Our approach combines SHAP values and LIME to explain the role of each feature in our classification model, revealing that age, comorbidities, and oxygen saturation levels are key indicators of ICU admission. Consequently, we recommend focusing on elderly patients with underlying health conditions and compromised oxygen levels to ensure timely ICU allocation.

In this study, we examine the eigenfunctions of the transmission eigenvalue problem within a transmission eigenvalue problem framework in $\mathbb{R}^N$. We consider a scenario where the transmission eigenvalue parameters within a 3D ball exhibit non-constant variations. Our analysis reveals that when the transmission eigenvalue parameters maintain constant values, significant localization of the eigenfunctions occurs near the surface of the ball. Furthermore, when the transmission eigenvalue parameters experience minimal fluctuations, localized transmission eigenfunctions persist near the surface of the ball.

This paper presents a novel, multi-task pre-training strategy that significantly enhances the field of spoken language processing. By leveraging a large dataset of spoken text, we can develop a robust, comprehensive spoken language representation. Our proposed framework combines several tasks, including text-to-speech generation, speech recognition, and a newly introduced metric that measures the similarity between utterances, to optimize spoken language representations. Through extensive experiments on spoken language understanding tasks, we demonstrate that this pre-training strategy yields notable improvements over existing models, ultimately achieving state-of-the-art performance.

The universal bundle functor, which maps a simplicial group to its universal bundle, induces a monad on the category of simplicial groups, with the monad's associated paramodoidle being a monoid object in the category of simplicial groups, equipped with a left action by the monad. Research by Porter revealed that this paramodoidle is isomorphic to the simplicial group of automorphisms of the universal bundle of a pointed simplicial set, which we now provide an alternative proof for.

The number of subgroups within a finite group G, denoted as $s_G$, is analyzed in terms of its magnitude in terms of G's order, $|G|$. We demonstrate that $s_G$ is bounded above by $|G|^{3\log^{*}|G|+O(1)}$, where the logarithmic terms and constant are defined. This result implies a polynomial bound of the form $s_G \leq |G|^{C+\epsilon}$ for an arbitrarily small positive value $\epsilon$ and a constant $C$. We also examine the structure of groups that achieve the maximum number of subgroups, revealing a specific composition in terms of their Sylow subgroups and a specific type of group known as the symmetric group.

We derive a continuous form of the Hirota-Kimura system's discrete self-adjointness, which in the limit mirrors the property of the continuous system's self-adjointness in Hirota's bilinear method. By examining the discrete $S^{(1,0)}$ variable, we find its continuum limit is described by the Korteweg-de Vries equation, and similarly, the discrete $R$ variable's continuum limit is described by the modified Korteweg-de Vries equation.

Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) faces a significant challenge due to the scarcity of object-object relationship data, which hinders effective model optimization. Current approaches often rely on balanced sampling techniques to mitigate the impact of noisy proposals, but they fall short in delivering satisfactory results. To address this issue, we introduce a novel optimization strategy, Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), which selectively filters out uninformative object-centric negative proposals, thereby enhancing the optimization of both relationship prediction and object detection components. Additionally, we propose a new proposal sampling method that leverages scene semantics to capture more relevant object interactions. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of BNPS, yielding a substantial improvement of 2.8 mAP on the V-RelDet dataset, and also exhibit strong generalization capabilities across various models and proposal sampling methods.

A key aspect of quantum mechanics, the unpredictability of outcomes, is essential for its fundamental understanding and practical applications. However, the act of observing this unpredictability is often complicated by environmental interference. Our research demonstrates that the act of partially measuring a quantum system can actually isolate its remaining quantum characteristics. We have found that partially measuring the system's state with respect to its pure state effectively extracts its residual quantum behavior. This can be achieved by using the post-measurement state, which retains some level of quantum unpredictability. We have also found that partially measuring the system's evolution with respect to its initial state with an ancillary system also effectively isolates the system's residual quantum behavior. This can be achieved by using the final state of the ancillary system, which retains some level of quantum unpredictability. Our findings provide a method to study the quantum behavior of a quantum system without the need for full collapse of its state.

This research introduces a novel social relationship representation method, which dynamically updates the connections within a social network graph in real-time. By leveraging the historical social relationships of individuals, our approach allows for the incorporation of past relationships into the social relationship representation. This is achieved through the use of Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to update the social relationships, which are initially encoded using Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). The effectiveness of this representation in predicting individual social actions is demonstrated through experiments conducted on two large-scale social networks, which revealed a significant improvement in predictive accuracy compared to a baseline model.

We introduce a novel graph-based neural network architecture, the adaptive graph neural network (AGNN), designed to dynamically adjust computation based on input data. By selectively sampling nodes in a graph, AGNN reduces the computational burden on GPU hardware, while maintaining efficiency. We then develop an adaptive sampling method that optimizes the trade-off between performance and computation, and apply it to cat pose estimation in video data. The results show that AGNN outperforms static models in terms of accuracy, and surpasses other adaptive neural networks, with gains of up to 10% in computational efficiency and 2% in accuracy.

This research focuses on the development of a comprehensive framework for generating high-quality Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) circuits, which are essential building blocks in digital signal processing systems. Our innovative approach builds upon an existing exact multiplierless synthesis tool by integrating the concept of error propagation, enabling the creation of MCM circuits that balance accuracy and efficiency. By incorporating error propagation rules into the synthesis process, we can identify optimal intermediate values and reduce the overall circuit complexity. Our proposed solution also incorporates specialized modules for addition, subtraction, and absolute value operations, which are crucial in MCM circuit implementations. Experimental results demonstrate the practical applicability and effectiveness of our framework in producing MCM circuits with improved precision and efficiency.

A rapidly evolving field, quantum deep learning, has garnered significant interest due to its potential to integrate quantum computing and machine learning. Nevertheless, it still faces significant challenges in practice, particularly in accessing quantum hardware and the limited understanding of quantum neural networks. To address these issues, we present a comprehensive review of quantum deep learning, highlighting its current limitations and promising prospects. Our analysis focuses on the fundamental aspects of quantum computing and neural networks, as well as the applications of quantum deep learning in scientific research.

The development of radio frequency technology has been primarily driven by high energy physics, yet its applications have also expanded to other types of accelerators, such as those used in free electron lasers, neutron sources, medical treatments, and industrial processes.

A high energy Muon Collider, with the potential to reach a center of mass energy of 10 TeV, is an attractive option for future particle physics research. However, its practical realization poses significant engineering and technological challenges. This document outlines the essential physics and engineering hurdles associated with its operation, as well as potential advancements in technology that could be developed. The document also discusses the potential for a Muon Collider to be built as a standalone facility or as an integrated component of a combined Muon Collider and Muon-Rhon Collider complex.

We analyze the dispersion patterns of scalar and vector modes in a relativistic fluid that exhibits viscosity, within the context of Einstein's equations perturbed at first order. Our findings confirm that the fluid-based approach yields the same dispersion relations as those obtained through kinetic theory and hydrodynamics at their respective applicable levels. Additionally, we contrast our results with recent hydrodynamic models that incorporate dissipation at a specific order.

We've investigated the Hawking radiation emitted by primordial black holes, specifically focusing on their photon, graviton, and antiphoton emissions. Our analysis is based on the full, non-relativistic treatment of Hawking radiation, taking into account the complete thermal distribution of radiated particles. We found that the peak of this Hawking radiation occurs at different energies depending on the mass of the black hole. For black holes with smaller masses, the peak radiation is in the form of low-energy photons, resulting in a significantly higher overall photon flux compared to antiphoton flux. We also found that the ratio of emitted gravitons to photons is constant, regardless of the mass of the black hole. Our calculations show that the total number of emitted particles, including gravitons and photons, is on the order of 3.73 times greater for gravitons than for photons.

This study presents a novel, high-speed processor architecture designed for the rapid evaluation of complex circuits, incorporating both Boolean and arithmetic operators. By pipeline processing, our design achieves a significant speedup, allowing each clock cycle to process one circuit operation. We propose an innovative processor design featuring a customized instruction set, pipelined structure, and advanced circuit components. By optimizing circuit design and eliminating redundant logic, our processor demonstrates high efficiency and speed in its current form.

Our research demonstrates that a constant-time polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) exists for a broad class of crisp constraint problems. This PTAS can handle any problem that involves minimizing costs associated with general-valued constraints. Additionally, we found that this scheme is efficient, requiring a time complexity of $O(n^{1+\epsilon})$, where $\epsilon$ is a small positive value that can be adjusted. This approximation scheme is versatile and can be applied to various domains, including general-valued and hybrid CSPs, as well as mixed integer optimization problems.

Recent breakthroughs in few-shot sequence-to-sequence tasks have been achieved by leveraging external memory, such as lexical or semantic information, to supplement syntactic structure. However, the self-contained sequence trees necessary for few-shot parsing are often computationally expensive to annotate. To address this issue, we introduce FPIO, a few-shot parsing model that relies on a self-contained outer product immersion network to generate accurate parse trees efficiently. Through extensive experiments on the Penn Treebank dataset with a range of tree sizes and annotation levels, we demonstrate that FPIO outperforms existing few-shot parsing methods when trained with annotated data, and achieves comparable results to those methods trained with golden standard datasets. Furthermore, our analysis reveals the significance of accurate tree generation in few-shot parsing and the potential of incorporating erroneous syntactic structures into few-shot training. To facilitate further research, we provide the source code and dataset at https://github.com/stevenjgao/FPIO.

This study introduces a novel semantic segmentation task for aerial hyperspectral images, leveraging the high-level categories from the Hyperion dataset. We've developed a set of precise labels through a combination of segmentation and spectral analysis, which are then utilized to enhance the segmentation process. Our investigation focuses on the impact of these refined labels on the segmentation performance, as well as the optimal ways to incorporate them into the learning process. We've developed and tested two distinct approaches to leverage the auxiliary labels, which outperform a baseline method by significant margins, achieving improvements of 10.4% and 5.3% respectively, according to the intersection over union metric.

A 2019 study by the TESS mission revealed an unusual pattern in the rotation of a specific star, KIC 9267654, which is an F-type star located 1,100 light-years away. This star, which is 1.4 times more massive than our Sun, exhibits distinct rotation speeds at different latitudes. To understand this phenomenon, we conducted a detailed analysis of the star's characteristics, including its temperature, mass, and age, using various computational models. We also examined the star's brightness variations over time, which are caused by large dark spots on its surface. Our findings suggest that the star's rotation pattern could be explained by the presence of spots at different latitudes, which are moving across the star's surface as it rotates. This would result in different brightness variations at different times, which are consistent with the observed pattern in the star's rotation.

We propose an innovative RAM model that accommodates polynomial integers, allowing for any number of bits as needed. We demonstrate that a polynomial-speed algorithm in this model can be efficiently translated into a circuit with nearly the same time complexity and only a slight increase in data storage requirements. We also show that this translation can be achieved with nearly the same number of steps and data accesses, and with a circuit depth that is only logarithmically larger. We further establish that this translation can be efficiently achieved with a circuit with nearly the same time complexity and a data storage increase of only a constant factor. In recent years, session-based recommendation systems have gained significant attention due to their ability to provide accurate and real-time recommendations. A key challenge in developing these systems is the need for substantial session data, which is often limited. Traditional data augmentation techniques have been employed to overcome this limitation, but they often rely on manual adjustments and lack a unified approach. In this study, we introduce a novel, self-supervised method for session-based recommendation that learns effective data transformations through unsupervised learning. Our framework utilizes a session as a sequence of items and employs a memory module to capture item relationships, which are then used to predict the next item in the session. To improve representation and enable data augmentation, we develop a geometric-based method that generates similar sessions and propose a contrastive learning objective to learn robust session embeddings. Our approach outperforms existing methods and achieves superior results on real-world datasets.

This research builds upon the 2019 study by S. Mesnager et al., which introduced a method for constructing linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from specific group ring elements. We expand on their work by developing families of LCD code subgroups derived from group ring elements with tailored polynomials and coefficients, with conditions that can be adjusted to yield various LCD code properties. Furthermore, we present several newly created binary LCD code families, with support in calculating the maximum possible dimension of certain classes of group-subgroup generated LCD codes.

The real cohomology of a Lie group is isomorphic to the exterior algebra generated by invariant differential forms. These invariant forms serve as a connecting link between a Lie group's real cohomology and its invariant differential forms. A key challenge in this context is determining a specific basis of invariant differential forms that represent the cohomology ring. Previous studies have addressed this issue for the special linear group through an approach utilizing Clifford modules. This paper extends this method to the general linear group, $\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}$, and demonstrates that the exterior algebra of its cohomology ring can be spanned by a specific set of invariant forms derived from a particular differential form on the sphere.

We propose a new architecture for visual categorization, using a modified recurrent neural network. The original recurrent structure is designed to be both computationally efficient and adaptable to different types of data. The network is trained using unsupervised data, and its performance is assessed on a large-scale object recognition benchmark. The results show that the architecture can learn to distinguish between objects effectively, and that its performance is comparable to state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks. The analysis of the recurrent structure's behavior reveals the importance of additional input variables, which can be used to improve the understanding of the data.

The skin effect, a hallmark of non-Hermitian systems, is examined in a non-Hermitian version of the Hatano-Nelson chain with added internal connections. We find that the skin effect, initially observed in the simplest form of this chain, is actually influenced by correlations when they are present. The skin effect, however, can be reproduced in the large system limit using a method that considers only the average behavior.

A quaternary Golay complementary array pair (QGCAP) is an arrangement of sensors in a line with specific properties that minimize interference in signal processing. This research presents a new method for generating QGCAPs of optimal length, which can be applied to the development of QGCAPs based on a recursive technique. The resulting QGCAPs based on this method can be used to create feasible QGCAPs of specific lengths. Additionally, this study provides a comprehensive catalog of QGCAPs based on a ternary system for lengths up to 100 and derives a formula to determine the minimum possible length of QGCAPs. The findings in this paper also have implications for the creation of feasible QGCAPs of certain lengths.

Recent measurements of the Higgs boson's properties from the LHC experiments have been analyzed, specifically its coupling with vector bosons. Based on the latest data, we determined the constraints on the Higgs boson's coupling strength, which are expressed as anomalous vector boson couplings. These constraints are expressed in terms of the Higgs boson's coupling constant, which is normalized to the standard model prediction. The anomalous couplings are constrained to be less than a few percent of the standard model prediction, which is consistent with the standard model prediction.

Change detection is a crucial task in remote sensing that can be accomplished without supervision by learning a data-driven representation of normal changes and flagging areas where the scene has significantly changed. However, detecting changes in land cover on a large scale remains a challenging problem due to the difficulty in distinguishing between changes in land cover and normal changes. In this study, we introduce an innovative approach to unsupervised change detection in remote sensing images that utilizes a novel unsupervised segmentation method to identify areas where the scene has significantly changed. Through experiments, we demonstrate that our proposed unsupervised change detection method can effectively identify changes in land cover and outperform existing methods in scenarios where the scene has undergone a substantial change. Additionally, we find that our method also excels in detecting changes in land cover even when the scene has undergone a moderate change, surpassing existing methods that rely on supervised learning with labeled data in certain cases.

We have established that for any positive integer n, the maximum number of ways n can be expressed as the sum of four squares from the set {0,1,...,r-1} is limited to 2r^4 times a constant. This finding significantly improves upon earlier estimates, and we also discuss the potential applications of this constant in relation to the representation of numbers as sums of squares.

The ability to control the Heisenberg spin exchange interaction between two electron spins in a silicon lattice is crucial for the development of large-scale spin qubit systems. Using a combination of advanced techniques, researchers have found that embedding a single dopant atom near the surface of a silicon wafer allows for efficient coupling between electron and nuclear spins through the hyperfine interaction. This enables the transfer of a spin state from one electron to another with high fidelity, even over a distance of 10 nanometers. Furthermore, the study found that the nuclear spin can be used to mediate the exchange interaction, allowing for the creation of a spin state that is synchronized between two electron spins and lasts for a significant period of time.

We introduce LibOPT, an open-source C library that provides a collection of benchmarking functions and optimization algorithms. The library includes 92 benchmarking functions and 12 optimization algorithms, which can be utilized in various ways, including as standalone programs, a command-line interface, and a Python interface. We present the library's design and implementation details, along with a plan for its ongoing development.
We have calculated the transitivity degree for complete toric algebraic and affine varieties over an arbitrary field.

This paper explores the momentum characteristics of multi-particle systems within non-abelian quantum mechanics, an area that has received relatively little attention. We examine the momentum distribution of the entire system, individual particles, and the momentum's effect on the wave function, all within the context of multi-particle momentum quantum states.

This study investigates the impact of two-photon absorption on a semiconductor's charge carrier dynamics, which is crucial for its nonlinear optical properties. A mathematical model based on a system of partial differential equations is developed to describe charge carrier behavior, and its long-term dynamics are analyzed in the context of a 3D space. A previously unexplored variable transformation is introduced to facilitate the analysis, and it is demonstrated that this new variable's behavior is bounded in a specific space. Furthermore, it is shown that the original model's solutions exhibit stable properties within a 3D space, and under the condition of no initial charge carriers, it is proven that the photon density's stable properties within a 3D space are also present.

We introduce a novel, 2.7 billion parameter model, MARBERT, which is adept at recognizing various forms of hate speech, including misogyny, by leveraging contextual information and incorporating a gender bias dataset. Our experimental results demonstrate that MARBERT outperforms existing models in multiple languages, including Spanish, English, and German.

The standard quadratic ESPDE can be viewed as a type of backward stochastic differential equation with a specific constraint on its generator, which depends only on current values. This study broadens the definition to include a quadratic stochastic differential equation with memory, and under certain conditions, it's possible to prove the existence and uniqueness of a solution based on a known GSDE solution.

Reinforcement learning has shown great promise in developing robust control systems, but its practical application is often hindered by the complexity of fully specifying a simulation environment. To address this, we developed a novel method that learns a dynamics model with an enforced minimum level of noise in the predictive output. By incorporating this constraint into the learning process, we are able to produce a more realistic model that generalizes well to different settings and produces a more reliable controller. Our results show that the method yields a controller that is more resilient to unexpected changes in the environment, as well as in a range of long-term predictive tasks.

The proposed framework for analyzing coded caching schemes is presented, which draws a connection between the caching strategies and specific sets of points within a projective geometry, represented as combinatorial objects, which in turn guarantee the optimal performance of the caching schemes, which are also linked to these sets of points as hypergraph coverings, which are further exemplified by specific objects, which are orthonormal arrays and algebraic geometry sets of points, respectively.

We propose a constructive and predicative set theory called Scott, designed to serve as a predicative framework for a Scott-type model of Martin-L\"of's Identity Type. We demonstrate that Scott-type models of ID can be utilized to construct a predicative framework in a predicative manner and that the resulting typeset is capable of being interpreted as a higher-order constructive and predicative set theory.

We've developed a refined formula for the constant term of degenerate Eisenstein series, extending it to all Weyl group segments. This new formula builds upon an earlier decomposition by Cogdell, Delaunay, and Jiang, which expressed the Eisenstein series as a sum over Weyl group classes. By utilizing this decomposition, we can derive an orthogonal decomposition, allowing us to express each class as a sum over relevant Weyl group cosets with distinct central terms. Ultimately, this refined formula serves as a crucial step in computing Rankin-Selberg L-function integrals involving products of Sp(n) and SP(n) irreducible representations.

This research focuses on enhancing collision avoidance strategies for mobile robotic arms by leveraging their spatial configuration, which is often overlooked in existing methods. We introduce a spatial structure-based collision avoidance technique that utilizes a novel metric to quantify the likelihood of collisions for multiple linked robots. Building upon this measure, we develop a method to determine safe movement parameters for the robots, which is then integrated into a control framework to prevent collisions. We extend our approach to handle scenarios involving multiple simultaneous obstacles and present simulation results demonstrating its effectiveness in navigating a Khepera III robot and an Epson SCARA arm around various obstacles.

The ability to convey meaning effectively, whether in written or spoken form, poses a significant challenge that natural language processing seeks to overcome.  This challenge is particularly pressing in light of the growing importance of text and speech in the digital age.  This paper outlines the fundamental concepts of text classification and generation, highlighting their relevance to broader applications of natural language processing.  It also discusses the key techniques and algorithms employed to tackle these problems, as well as the most promising areas for further research and development.

Quantum phase estimation is a vital tool in precision measurements, with Ramsey interferometry being a fundamental technique. Recent advances in Bose-Einstein condensates have enabled the creation of nonlinear phase rotations, which can now be utilized to develop a more sophisticated form of interferometry. This paper presents a quantum phase estimation algorithm based on a more complex Hadamard gate, which significantly improves upon the limitations of traditional methods. Our research demonstrates that this innovative approach can achieve better results than conventional RI, with the extent of its advantage depending on specific conditions. Moreover, this enhanced RI method can also achieve a level of precision beyond the standard quantum limit, with the potential to reach the Heisenberg limit under specific circumstances.

This paper explores the mappings of meromorphic type from a complex n-dimensional space to a complex space of the same dimension, while also considering k distinct hyperplanes within that space. We establish new criteria for when these mappings land entirely in a complex subspace of lower dimension, based on the number of intersections with the given hyperplanes. Our results expand upon existing ones for specific cases where n equals two.

This paper presents an innovative approach to calculating Gröbner bases by combining an existing algorithm with a metric that measures the size of polynomial systems. By leveraging this size measure, we can develop an effective method for prioritizing critical steps in the computation. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach on polynomial systems that are too complex for traditional methods.

This result indicates that the number of photons produced per unit of charged particle density is about 1.35. This finding is consistent with previous photon-π0 ratio measurements, suggesting that the number of photons produced per unit of charged particle density is about 1.35. The function exco_2(n,H) represents the maximum number of edges a K_4^3-free 3-uniform hypergraph with n vertices and infinite edge weights can have while containing hyperedges of weight 1. We will discuss several characteristics of exco_2(n,H) for specific triples of hyperedges in 3-uniform hypergraphs with 4 vertices, including its growth rate, structural form, and possible extensions to a broader class of hypergraphs with more vertices.

A widely used line rendering technique in computer graphics employs a fan shape for line joins, which is commonly seen in line charts and maps. However, rendering this shape can be costly, especially when utilizing high-quality rendering methods. We have developed a novel algorithm that significantly optimizes the rendering of fan-shaped line joins by eliminating unnecessary triangle rendering. The new algorithm can seamlessly integrate with existing line rendering methods, including those for straight lines, curved lines, and polyline rendering. Our approach has been tested on a sample program, which demonstrates a notable reduction in rendering overhead, yielding performance gains of up to 15% and 22% for curved and straight lines, respectively, along with improved rendering efficiency.

This study develops a quasi-interpolation formula on unstructured grids, based on the recently introduced positive rbf, which is derived from the thin sphere product of thin plate rbf and multiquadric rbf. The formula's accuracy can be adjusted by modifying its parameters, while maintaining convexity and monotonicity due to the inherent properties of the new rbf. The research demonstrates through numerical experiments that the new formula exhibits high precision in both stability and order.

The TeV gamma-ray and positron excesses observed in the Galactic Center region may be attributed to pulsar remnants emitting high-energy particles. To test this theory, we created a 3D model of the Galactic Center's pulsar population and their interaction with the surrounding environment. Our simulations show that the pulsar remnants' combined gamma-ray emission aligns with the observed excess, but the energy output is heavily influenced by the environment's characteristics. Furthermore, the simulated positron flux from these remnants is insufficient to account for the observed excess, particularly at close distances.

To enhance the accuracy of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in image classification, we developed a data augmentation technique called super pixel delimiting masks. This method leverages CNN-learned features to create diverse training samples, thereby increasing the robustness of the classifier. We applied this technique to the image classification problem and evaluated its effectiveness using the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets. By using super pixel delimiting masks, we achieved a 0.4% top-1 accuracy improvement on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-110, and a 0.7% accuracy gain on CIFAR-100 with the same network.

This study examines climate change discourse through a social network lens, analyzing the flow of information from the most influential sources. By applying an innovative approach, we investigated the four primary disciplines discussing climate change - economics, ecology, engineering, and earth sciences - to reveal the prevalence of climate change within each field. Our analysis of over 100,000 articles from leading journals in these disciplines shows climate change is a prominent topic in ecology and earth sciences, but less so in economics and engineering. Furthermore, climate change garners more interest among scientists and engineers than economists and is of greater concern to policymakers than general interest science publications and ecological scientists. Interestingly, the most influential scientists and policymakers are not necessarily the most prolific in publishing, but rather those who engage in dialogue with others.

Soft robotic systems are gaining attention due to their versatility and potential for novel applications. However, their complex nonlinear dynamics make them challenging to control. This paper proposes a new approach using the Koopman operator theory to develop an efficient control framework for complex nonlinear systems, particularly in soft robotics. We demonstrate the applicability of this approach through a simulation of a soft robotic arm, utilizing a data-driven reduced-order model and sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics. This method is then applied to design a linear observation operator and a spectral projection, enabling a controlled feedback system. Our results show that this approach can be used to achieve complex tasks, such as trajectory tracking and motion planning, in a data-driven manner.

We've developed an innovative algorithm that leverages the geometric properties of probability distributions to accelerate optimization processes. This new method, known as Natural Gradient Descent, outperforms standard optimization techniques by taking into account the curvature of the loss landscape, resulting in faster convergence. To implement this algorithm, we've devised a efficient way to calculate matrix inverses using Cholesky decomposition, which also provides benefits for Bayesian inference and other applications. Our implementation has been shown to be particularly effective when used with neural networks that utilize ReLU activation functions.

We have conducted a detailed analysis of the $J$-band imaging data from the CEERS survey, focusing on the 1023-J022630.50+572254.2 object at a redshift of approximately 6.6. This source exhibits unusual characteristics, including a compact, reddish appearance and an extended bluish feature. Our investigation into its spectral properties using the NIRSpec IFU data revealed that its spectrum is characterized by strong [O III] $\lambda$5007 and H$\beta$ emission lines, as well as a continuum that is heavily reddened. This object is likely an active galactic nucleus, given its high-ionization emission lines and low metal content, and its compact nature suggests it is a point source. The bluish feature surrounding this source is spatially distinct and has a redshift of approximately 6.6, with a red spectrum dominated by a strong H$\alpha$ emission line. This feature is likely a jet or a tidal tail associated with the active galactic nucleus, and its presence suggests that active galactic nuclei can drive outflows that extend far beyond the nucleus itself.

Predicting a patient's survival time is crucial for medical treatment planning, but the limited availability of longitudinal data hinders the development of accurate models. To address this issue, we propose Lite-ProSENet, a novel method that utilizes only the first and last pathology slides from each patient to infer intermediate pathology states. By combining these pathology images with clinical data, we can effectively predict a patient's survival time. Our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and is particularly effective for lung cancer patients.

In recent years, deep learning models have achieved impressive results, yet their internal workings remain largely inaccessible. To improve interpretability, we developed a new approach that uses language to explain the statistical state representations learned during a task. By combining these findings with data-driven analysis, we can identify key features that inform the models' decisions. Our results show that this method is effective at uncovering meaningful patterns in the models, which can be used to generate more understandable explanations for their behavior.

We've developed a method to build an accurate, precise and unbiased reconstruction of the 3D power spectrum from BAO data, using information from multiple surveys with varying redshifts and bin sizes. Our approach is demonstrated through simulations of BAO data from the DESI survey, incorporating real-world complexities such as survey limitations and forecasted BAO scale uncertainties. Our results show that the proposed reconstruction accurately accounts for non-linear effects and shot noise, and that the precision of the power spectrum is survey-dependent, peaking at shorter wavelengths and lower redshifts. Our full 3D power spectrum approach outperforms traditional methods based on BAO distances alone, particularly at higher redshifts where BAO measurements are more limited.

This research paper establishes a criterion for the irreducibility of tensor products formed by a highest weight module over an infinite-dimensional Lie superalgebra U(𝕙)-free module in an arbitrary characteristic. The criterion is expressed in terms of isomorphism and relies on the properties of the constituent highest weight modules and U(𝕙)-free modules.

This paper presents a novel approach to classifying the sentiment of tweets by leveraging an Long-Short Term Memory model. We utilize preprocessed data and word embeddings to enhance the model's performance. The study builds upon existing research, which has demonstrated the effectiveness of LSTM in sentiment analysis tasks. We start by examining prior studies that employed Long Short Term Memory networks for sentiment analysis, then outline our methodology, which includes data preprocessing and the construction of an LSTM-based classifier. The results of our experiment demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a high level of accuracy in identifying the sentiment of tweets.

The quality of natural conversations depends heavily on the dialogue system's ability to adhere to its role constraints.  Current methods for role-based dialogue typically rely on extensive human annotations, which are both costly and impractical to obtain.  In an effort to overcome these limitations, we propose a new approach that automatically generates role specifications based on written text, which can then be used to improve a dialogue system's responses.  By fine-tuning a language model using these specifications, we enable it to effectively follow its assigned role in various situations.  Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline approaches and achieves comparable results to role-specific systems that were manually designed.

A new type of gravitational wave background, known as stochastic memory background, has been discovered, which behaves differently from traditional stochastic backgrounds. Unlike conventional backgrounds that diminish at higher frequencies, the stochastic memory background remains constant across a wide frequency range, from 10^-3 Hz to 100 Hz. This unique memory effect can be triggered by significant events, such as the formation of massive black holes, which impart a lasting imprint on spacetime curvature. The memory background's amplitude can be estimated using the equation: S_Ω^h_mem (f) = C_mem f^(1/3) (f/70 Hz)^(2/3), where C_mem is a measure of its intensity. This memory background's presence can be detected by LISA through its distinct spectral signature, which can be mistaken for a cosmological signal. To accurately interpret data, it's crucial to differentiate between the cosmological and memory contributions, which can be achieved by analyzing their distinct frequency dependencies.

We're investigating a scenario where supersymmetry breaking is mediated by gauge interactions, which also offers a solution to the hierarchy problem. Our proposed model of heavy neutrino decay, involving supersymmetric particles, can result in leptogenesis at a PeV scale, an idea that was previously considered unfeasible. The neutrinos responsible for generating mass are connected to a gauge-mediated supersymmetry breaking sector through a portal of right-handed neutrino interactions. This model naturally produces the required right-handed neutrino couplings through supersymmetric particle interactions, specifically involving smuons and charginos, all while adhering to current experimental constraints.

We propose a new semantic communication system that allows for more efficient data transmission by focusing on conveying essential meaning rather than exact numerical values. To achieve this, we have developed a novel framework that utilizes a data compression technique based on clustering, which enables the preservation of essential information in a compact format. Our approach is unique in that it does not rely on prior knowledge at the receiving end, and instead uses a data-driven method to optimize transmission based on a predefined semantic goal. We have evaluated the performance of our system in various wireless environments and found that it offers improved reliability and energy efficiency while maintaining the desired level of meaning at a higher rate than traditional communication methods.

This study introduces a new approach to creating a word suggestion system that offers more precise suggestions by integrating both semantic and syntactic analysis methods. Our hybrid model surpasses standalone syntactic and semantic models in accuracy, as demonstrated by a 10% and 14% improvement in precise word recovery on the CS229N 2018n spam comment dataset, respectively. Additionally, we developed a user-friendly interface that enables the evaluation of our model's performance through a real-world application.

Recent advancements in attention networks have shown great potential in enhancing
recurrent networks by enabling them to focus on key aspects of the input data.
This paper proposes a novel application of attention networks in the realm of
recommendation systems by developing an attention-based recurrent neural network
that can effectively rank relevant items. Unlike traditional methods that utilize
user and item features, our approach incorporates user feedback as the primary
input, allowing the model to capture more nuanced aspects of user behavior.
Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our method in producing more
accurate recommendation lists.

We present a novel design for large-scale treadmilling devices composed of two interconnected circular elements. The internal structure features asymmetric propellers, enabling controlled movement along a surface when exposed to a fluid in an energy-rich state. Our simulations reveal that the dimer's motion is similar to being steered by a wheel, allowing for directional navigation. The proposed device demonstrates the potential for guiding its movement through external forces acting on the wheel-like component, as well as more complex navigation via feedback systems, and may have applications in delivering materials to specific locations.

This study presents a novel approach for modeling fractured porous media, combining the Stokes equations with Darcy's law to describe fluid flow in pores and fracture lines. To ensure accurate numerical results, we utilize a high-quality conforming Delaunay tetrahedral mesh that precisely intersects with fracture surfaces. Our fully coupled algorithm employs a fixed-stress split method, which is then accelerated by the additive Schur complement preconditioned conjugate gradient technique. To validate our model, we compare our results with analytical solutions and examine a realistic case involving a confined aquifer and an aquitard, along with a corresponding 3D simulation.

This paper presents a novel approach to designing control systems for drone
ensembles that maintain a specific geometric configuration. The proposed
algorithm ensures that the average position of the drones remains at a fixed
position, which is crucial for maintaining stability. By keeping the average
position stable, the design enhances the efficiency of drone operations,
facilitates the integration of drone groups with stationary equipment, and
enables the development of scalable control systems that remain effective
across a range of drone counts. The proposed algorithm is demonstrated to be
effective through simulations of a particular drone geometric arrangement,
which is scaled up to illustrate its versatility.

We investigate the eigenvalue -1 in the Seidel matrix of a connected chain graph, demonstrating that it is always an eigenvalue. Furthermore, we identify the eigenvector corresponding to eigenvalue -1 and explore its implications for the Seidel spectrum of a connected chain graph, along with a characterization of a class of chain graphs whose Seidel matrices possess a specific eigenvalue -r.

This research investigates the existence of solutions to stochastic control problems with time delays, specifically focusing on a model of geometric stochastic control with delayed times. We establish sufficient conditions for the existence of solutions to these problems and demonstrate that solutions may not exist when attempting to find a delayed optimal investment and consumption strategy in a Black-Scholes model with a time lag.

The solution to the Dirac operator eigenvalue problem in a specific coordinate system, with a singular boundary in two dimensions, can be linked to Heun's equation and a specific type of matrix eigenvalue problem. By utilizing a matrix representation, the eigenvalue problem can be reformulated as a eigenvalue problem involving a tridiagonal matrix, allowing for efficient numerical solutions through the application of standard algorithms.

This research paper investigates a vehicle-to-vehicle communication system operating within a complex environment of multiple base stations and vehicles, where the latter act as temporary data transmitters. To effectively manage data transmission, we develop a scheduling system that optimizes base station assignments and vehicle selection based on pre-established agreements. This strategic approach leads to the creation of a performance evaluation system, which we then use to assess the average data transmission efficiency of the network. To further enhance this performance, we design a vehicle selection algorithm that maximizes efficiency, and our findings reveal that the strategic agreements between base stations and data transmission significantly boost the network's communication capacity. Additionally, we demonstrate that our algorithm's computational requirements scale linearly with the number of base stations in the network.

This paper outlines a novel, semi-supervised method for identifying sentence-level
annotations in Wikipedia articles. The proposed technique leverages the insights
gained from the activities of Wikipedia contributors who enhance and modify
individual sentences. By employing this method, it's possible to create a
substantial, automatically annotated data set that can be utilized to fine-tune
a language model's ability to evaluate sentence quality. The results demonstrate
that the language model trained using this method outperforms existing benchmarks
in a sentence annotation task.

Our proposed method, decision-based black-box knowledge distillation (DB3), differs from conventional knowledge distillation by exploiting the black-box model's output labels and adversarial examples, which are generated using white-box access. We have developed a new approach to black-box distillation that bypasses the need for gradient information. This method leverages the responses of the adversary to refine its output, while also utilizing perturbations to extract additional insights. We have demonstrated the effectiveness of DB3 through experiments on image classification, where it achieved superior performance compared to existing methods, including white-box models, using a relatively small number of queries.

Using a dataset of 36.1 fb^-1 collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV by the LHCb experiment, we have studied the decays of the D*+ particle into a K^- and a B_s^0. The analysis is based on the D*+ tag from D*+ -> D^0 pi_s^+ and D^0 -> K^- K^+ or D^0 -> K^- pi^+ pi^0, resulting in the observation of D*+ -> K^- B_s^0 in four distinct mass ranges for the D^0 tag. The branching fractions for the D^0 -> K^- K^+ and D^0 -> K^- pi^+ pi^0 decays are found to be (69.44 +/- 1.10 +/- 1.10)% and (94.77 +/- 1.23 +/- 1.23)%, respectively, with the uncertainties stemming from statistical and systematic sources.

The presence of continuous trace algebras within a string theory background's D-brane spectrum can be used to identify the background as possessing a conventional T-dual. We develop a method for identifying these algebraic structures in string theory, focusing on classical D-branes that are classified by their K-theory properties. By incorporating this criterion, our analysis reveals that some heterotic string theory backgrounds can exhibit a Type I D-brane spectrum with continuous trace elements, implying the existence of a TYPE I/T-duality partner for the heterotic background.

Reinforcement learning has made significant advancements in recent years, with its application expanding to tasks that were previously thought to be unachievable. However, its application is often limited due to the need for substantial expert interaction, which can be costly and time-consuming. To overcome this limitation, Co-Imitation Learning (CoIL) has been developed as a novel approach that leverages agent-agent learning to reduce the need for expert involvement. CoIL allows agents to learn from each other's experiences, with one agent focusing on exploration and the other on exploitation, thereby achieving better results than traditional methods that rely on expert demonstrations. To facilitate efficient communication between agents, a novel message-passing mechanism has been designed, enabling them to share knowledge and improve their performance. CoIL has been successfully applied to a complex 3D manipulation task, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing the need for expert involvement and improving overall performance.

We've developed an upper limit on the likelihood of sequential decoding errors when using polarized cutoff rates as bias values, which allows us to determine the sequential decoding exponent under these conditions. This research also examines how choosing polarized cutoff rates impacts the probability of decoding errors.

This paper presents a novel, real-time hand tracking method based on a
monocular RGB camera that effectively handles common issues such as occlusion,
fingertip tracking, and object interaction. At the core of the algorithm is a
combination of an optical flow tracker and a segmentation network that utilizes
a small amount of manual annotation to achieve high accuracy. The approach
requires minimal data collection and can be quickly adapted to new objects with
just a few frames. The system successfully tracks hands even when occluded and
enables interaction with objects, all while operating at a fast rate of 30-60
frames per second. The approach has been tested on both real-world data and
simulated environments, and the results show its effectiveness and ease of use.

In this paper, we determine the complete classification of certain reduced groups over a finite field whose elements have a square equal to their own value, based on their integral properties. Our results show that these complete reduced groups correspond exactly to a specific family, denoted as $\mathcal{F}_{p,n}$, with each member having $n$ components and being formed by combining elements from a specific set of values, with each set's size being $n$ and each component being either $0$ or $1$.

A novel, end-to-end method for end-effector positioning is presented, utilizing a depth sensor for data acquisition. This streamlined process for joint calibration incorporates an adaptive Kalman filter to reduce measurement inaccuracies. By leveraging depth information, the system achieves more reliable data collection, thereby enhancing the robustness of the calibration. Furthermore, the Depth-Assisted approach yields superior results compared to its vision-based counterpart, particularly in scenarios involving noisy data.

In the context of network interference, choosing the right entities and designing effective data collection methods are crucial for accurately identifying and measuring it. We've developed a new method for pinpointing interference in a network, which relies on specific information about the experiment's setup. This approach allows us to pinpoint the most relevant entities for analysis and, consequently, improves the accuracy of detecting interference. We've also developed a new metric to quantify interference in the data, which enables researchers to identify which entities are susceptible to interference and, in turn, helps to improve detection capabilities. We've tested our method using simulated data and found that it can successfully identify interference in scenarios where traditional methods fail.

The existence of self-annihilating dark matter within the core of a neutron star has significant implications for its thermal evolution. If such an occurrence is to be possible, the resulting dark matter's annihilation and subsequent production of heat-carrying particles will lead to the emission of excess thermal radiation. This phenomenon will cause a neutron star to cool at a faster rate than it would otherwise, an effect that can be observed and potentially provide insight into the properties of dark matter.

We introduce ShapePipe, a novel pipeline that accurately measures galaxy shapes for weak-lensing studies. This open-source pipeline leverages the power of deep learning to produce shape estimates, along with an assessment of their reliability, by training on simulated galaxies. ShapePipe's shape estimates are derived from galaxy images using a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network, which is then refined through an analysis of bias and scatter in simulated data. The pipeline's reliability metric is determined by matching observed shape estimates to simulations, allowing for the identification of galaxies with reliable shape measurements. ShapePipe has been successfully tested on the COSMOS dataset, demonstrating its ability to accurately recover galaxy shapes while maintaining a high level of reliability.
